channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Nearly Half of Children in Kazakhstan Access Internet Before Age 8, UNICEF Raises Concerns
item.description: UNICEF reports that nearly half of children in Kazakhstan go online before the age of 8, with 46% of 9-17 year olds first accessing the internet between 5 and 8 years old. While digital technologies offer learning benefits, UNICEF highlights the need for child protection in the digital environment.

item.title: Afghan Transit: Why Chinese Investment is Stalled and How Kazakh Companies Can Profit
item.description: The article explores the reasons behind the stagnation of Chinese investment in Afghan transit and identifies opportunities for Kazakh companies to benefit. It analyzes the complexities of the Afghan transit corridor and suggests strategies for local businesses to capitalize on the situation.

item.title: Tajikistan and World Bank Discuss Export Development and Launch of 'Export School'
item.description: Tajikistan's Export Agency and the World Bank Group mission discussed the implementation of a supplier and export development program for 2026-2028 and the launch of an 'Export School'. The initiative aims to enhance export activities, strengthen domestic suppliers, and equip entrepreneurs with practical export knowledge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims for 100% High-Speed Internet Coverage by 2029, Ministry Reports
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development plans to achieve 100% high-speed internet coverage by the end of 2029. The initiative involves fixed broadband to over 3,600 villages by 2027, grant subsidies for regional operators, satellite systems for remote areas, and mobile internet upgrades in settlements with over 250 people.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Explains New Social Benefits Philosophy Focused on Need
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov announced a reform of social security, shifting to a needs-based system starting next year. He stated that affluent individuals capable of self-support should not receive state aid. The goal is to provide a 'push' for recipients to become self-sufficient, allowing funds to be redirected to more critical areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Heating and Hot Water Tariffs by Approximately 30 Percent
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Construction and Housing and Communal Services has proposed new tariffs for centralized heating and hot water, set to take effect from November 1. Central heating tariffs may rise by about 30 percent, from 241.44 to 314 soums per square meter daily. Hot water tariffs are also expected to increase by a similar margin.

item.title: Health Inspectors Find Violations at RFMS School Cafeteria in Almaty Following Student Hospitalizations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has sent investigation materials regarding violations found at the RFMS school cafeteria in Almaty to law enforcement agencies. The inspection followed the hospitalization of several students. Findings included breaches in food storage, sampling, and catering organization. Disciplinary actions and disinfection measures have been implemented.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agriculture Minister Explains Reduced Funding for Farmers
item.description: The volume of funding for the agricultural sector in Kazakhstan is set to decrease to 88 billion tenge annually by 2028-2029. Agriculture Minister Aidarbek Saparov explained that the reduction is linked to increased production and export volumes. This follows a parliamentary inquiry questioning the decrease in preferential loans and guarantees for farmers.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Explains Social Support Reductions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that social support spending will be reduced by 2.5 trillion tenge over three years. This is part of a reform shifting from category-based support to needs-based assistance, aiming to save state funds. The reform is expected to be fully implemented by January 2027.

item.title: Taliban Reports Over 100 Migrant Families Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 162 families, totaling 698 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan. These returns occurred through various border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, and Pul-e Abrisham and Islam Qala in Nimroz.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allocate 2 Trillion Tenge from National Fund for 'Big Construction' in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to allocate 2 trillion tenge from the National Fund for a large-scale construction program in 2027. An additional 1.5 trillion tenge each will be transferred in 2028 and 2029. Funds will finance critical social and infrastructure projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Economy Ministry Predicts Inflation Reduction by 2029
item.description: Kazakhstan's inflation rate is projected to be between 7.5-9.5% in 2027 and 6-8% in 2028-2029, according to the Ministry of National Economy. The ministry aims for a gradual decrease in inflation over the next three years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Rejects European Proposal to Accept Migrants in Exchange for Labor Opportunities
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister announced the country's rejection of a European proposal to accept migrants from Afghanistan and Africa. In exchange, the European country offered employment opportunities for Kyrgyz citizens. The proposed terms were deemed unacceptable by the Kyrgyz government, which is prioritizing domestic labor needs over facilitating overseas employment programs.

item.title: Human Rights Watch Urges France to Halt Deportation Plans for Afghans
item.description: Human Rights Watch has called on France to suspend plans to deport Afghans, citing concerns that returnees could face persecution, torture, or other serious abuses in Afghanistan. The call follows confirmation of a "technical dialogue" between French authorities and the Taliban over the return of Afghan nationals deemed security risks.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister: Wealthy individuals should rely on themselves, not state aid.
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that state assistance should be reserved for those unable to support themselves. Wealthy citizens, he emphasized, must rely on their own resources. This was discussed during a Kurultai session reviewing the 2027-2029 republican budget. The government aims to reduce the budget deficit by increasing revenues and optimizing expenditures.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency Disrupts Cross-Border Drop-Farming Operations.
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency (AFM) has dismantled cross-border criminal groups using citizens' bank cards from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan for online casino payments. These groups operated 'drop farms,' networks of bank accounts facilitating illicit transactions. Foreign nationals were recruited to open accounts and provide SIM cards and phones for scheme operation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Save 700 Billion Tenge on Benefits to Reduce Budget Deficit.
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to save 700 billion tenge by reducing social benefits as part of its strategy to decrease the national budget deficit. This measure is part of a broader plan to manage government finances and reallocate resources. The specific details of which benefits will be reduced and the timeline for these changes are expected to be further elaborated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Rejects European Conditions on Labor Migration and Migrant Reception
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister stated the country will not negotiate with European nations to accept migrants from Afghanistan and Africa in exchange for facilitating labor migration for Kyrgyz citizens. While Kyrgyz nationals can seek work abroad independently, Bishkek will not engage in such conditional agreements. Migration patterns are shifting towards Turkey and the USA.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Tighten Regulations for Pawnshops and Collection Agencies
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market plans to strengthen requirements for pawnshops and collection agencies. Agencies systematically violating laws may be removed from the registry. Current regulations prohibit collectors from threatening debtors, harassing them, or disclosing debt information to third parties.

item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts Houthi missile targeting Al-Kharj province
item.description: The Saudi-led Arab coalition announced the interception and destruction of a Houthi-launched cruise missile aimed at Al-Kharj province. Coalition spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Maliki stated that air defense systems detected and neutralized the missile. This incident occurs amidst escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia using ballistic missiles and drones.

item.title: Kazakhstan may cut budget spending if economic situation worsens, says Deputy PM
item.description: Kazakhstan may reduce budget expenditures if the economic situation deteriorates, stated Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Serik Zhumangarin. He responded to parliamentary questions regarding discrepancies between government forecasts and those of international financial organizations. The government anticipates growth driven by manufacturing, trade, construction, and logistics.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Deputy PM Forecasts Oil Prices and Tenge Exchange Rate Scenarios
item.description: Kazakhstan's government has outlined three budget scenarios for 2027 based on oil prices. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin stated that in a pessimistic scenario, oil could drop to $50 per barrel, potentially pushing the dollar exchange rate to 520 tenge, with average annual economic growth at 3.2%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Rejects European Proposal to Host Afghan Refugees
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has declined a European Union offer to host Afghan refugees. The decision was made without providing specific reasons for the rejection. This move comes amid ongoing concerns about the refugee situation in the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Stop Welfare Payments to Wealthy Citizens, Saving Trillions
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to save 2.5 trillion tenge over three years by ending welfare payments to affluent citizens. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that from January 1, 2027, benefits will be allocated based on need, ensuring state support for those unable to provide for themselves.

item.title: Kazakh Government to Save Nearly 2.5 Trillion Tenge by Ending Payments to 'Affluent' Citizens
item.description: The Kazakh government intends to save approximately 2.5 trillion tenge over three years by canceling welfare payments and benefits for affluent citizens. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov announced that starting January 1, 2027, social support will be based on need, not category, ensuring funds are redirected to more critical areas.

item.title: Kazakhstan's General Prosecutor's Office Investigates 13 Criminal Cases for Ministry of Defense Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's General Prosecutor's Office is investigating 13 criminal cases related to negligence and violations within the Ministry of Defense. The probe was initiated following a presidential order for a comprehensive review. Investigations are ongoing to determine all circumstances and involved parties, with details withheld for investigative integrity.

item.title: US Secretary of State Blinken to Visit Uzbekistan for C5+1 Meeting and Business Delegation
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken will visit Uzbekistan from October 17-22 to participate in a C5+1 ministerial meeting focused on strategic cooperation in Central Asia. He will also lead a U.S. business delegation of over 200 representatives to strengthen trade and economic ties. The visit underscores enhanced U.S.-Central Asia relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Forecast: Oil Price at $70/barrel in Base Scenario for 2027-2029
item.description: Kazakhstan's socio-economic development forecast for 2027-2029 sets the base scenario oil price at $70 per barrel. Three variants are considered: optimistic ($85/barrel, 5.9% GDP growth), base ($70/barrel), and pessimistic ($50/barrel, 3.2% GDP growth). This aligns with reduced global oil price forecasts by international organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Exempt Transport and Logistics Centers from Property Taxes Until 2040
item.description: Uzbekistan has adopted a resolution to develop its transport and logistics system. Key targets include increasing annual capacity to 40 million tons and boosting logistics service exports to $3.5 billion by 2030. Several regions will specialize in logistics. Importantly, transport and logistics centers will be fully exempt from land and property taxes until 2040, provided they meet specific criteria.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon observes CSTO military exercises 'Skala-2026'
item.description: On October 13, 2026, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon visited a command post to observe the CSTO special exercise 'Skala-2026,' focused on preventing and responding to emergencies. The drills, held at Tajikistan's National Rescuer Training Ground, simulate responses to a devastating earthquake.

item.title: Nearly 100,000 people moved into Afghanistan from Iran and Pakistan in two weeks
item.description: The International Organization for Migration recorded almost 100,000 arrivals into Afghanistan from Iran and Pakistan between September 27 and October 10. Over 39,000 movements out of the country towards these neighbors were also registered. Deportation was a significant driver for returns from Iran, cited by 61% of surveyed arrivals.

item.title: One Person Dies as Flash Flood Sweeps Away Car in Qashqadaryo Region
item.description: A person died on October 13 when a flash flood swept away a car in the mountainous areas of Dehqonobod district, Qashqadaryo region. A short, heavy downpour caused the flood. The driver and a passenger were in the car when it was carried away by the strong current. The passenger's body was later found.

item.title: Uzbekistan Authorities Task Governors to Restore 3.7 Million Hectares of Pastures by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev has tasked regional governors with restoring 3.7 million hectares of pastures by 2027. Currently, only 40% of the country's 21.2 million hectares of pastures are effectively utilized. The initiative aims to enhance food security and livestock farming.

item.title: Tajikistan to Develop National Plan for Disability Rights Protection
item.description: Tajikistan has officially ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. A roundtable in Dushanbe discussed priority measures for its implementation, coordination among state bodies, and fulfillment of international obligations. The Ministry of Health and Social Protection stated this marks a new phase in state policy towards people with disabilities.

item.title: Russia Accuses Japan of Using Journalists to Undermine National Security
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry has accused Japan of utilizing journalists stationed in Russia to gather intelligence aimed at undermining Russia's security. Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova called these actions regrettable, noting increased tensions between Moscow and countries supporting Ukraine or condemning Russia's invasion.

item.title: Afghan Farmers Adopt Climate-Resilient Innovations for Food Security
item.description: Afghan farmers are adopting innovative methods like laser land-levelling and solar dryers to conserve water, reduce losses, and boost incomes, according to the FAO. Initiatives in Kunduz, Faryab, Paktia, and Takhar are helping over 23,000 families improve irrigation, create income for women, and preserve produce.

item.title: Dozens of Students Hospitalized in Almaty with Food Poisoning Symptoms
item.description: Forty-seven students from the Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty were hospitalized on October 12-13 with symptoms of acute intestinal infection. Eight more students are under medical observation at the school's dormitory. The school, dormitory, and canteen operations are temporarily suspended pending laboratory analysis.

item.title: Donkeys Essential for Healthcare Access in Remote Bamiyan Province, MSF Reports
item.description: Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) states that donkeys are often the sole means for patients in remote Bamiyan province to reach healthcare facilities due to transportation limitations. A pregnant woman recently traveled over four hours by donkey to an MSF-supported clinic for childbirth, facing the same arduous journey home. MSF highlights increasing healthcare access difficulties for women since the Taliban's return.

item.title: Four Uzbek Citizens Rescued from Difficult Situation in Vladivostok
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens who found themselves in a difficult situation in Vladivostok have been returned to their homeland. Air tickets to Tashkent were purchased for them using funds from the Migration Agency's fund. This initiative ensured their safe return to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Promotes Regional Cooperation Initiatives in Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively promoting initiatives in Central Asia aimed at fostering cooperation and opening new opportunities. Consultative meetings of Central Asian leaders facilitate regular alignment of positions on crucial regional issues. The dialogue has expanded to include national coordinators, agencies, regions, and business circles.
